{{Short description|Uniform polyhedron with dihedral symmetry}}
{{No footnotes|date=March 2025}}
[[Image:Pentagrammic antiprism.png|thumb|A [[pentagrammic antiprism]] is made of two regular [[pentagram]]s and 10 equilateral [[triangle]]s.]]
In [[geometry]], a '''prismatic uniform polyhedron''' is a [[uniform polyhedron]] with [[Dihedral symmetry in three dimensions|dihedral symmetry]]. They exist in two infinite families, the uniform [[Prism (geometry)|prisms]] and the uniform [[antiprism]]s. All have their vertices in parallel planes and are therefore [[prismatoid]]s.

== Vertex configuration and symmetry groups ==

Because they are [[isogonal figure|isogonal]] (vertex-transitive), their [[vertex arrangement]] uniquely corresponds to a [[Point groups in three dimensions|symmetry group]]. 

The difference between the prismatic and antiprismatic symmetry groups is that  '''D<sub>''p''h</sub>''' has the vertices lined up in both planes, which gives it a reflection plane perpendicular to its ''p''-fold axis (parallel to the {p/q} polygon); while '''D<sub>''p''d</sub>''' has the vertices twisted relative to the other plane, which gives it a rotatory reflection.  Each has ''p'' reflection planes which contain the ''p''-fold axis.

The '''D<sub>''p''h</sub>''' symmetry group contains [[Inversion in a point|inversion]] if and only if ''p'' is even, while '''D<sub>''p''d</sub>''' contains inversion symmetry if and only if ''p'' is odd.

== Enumeration ==
There are:

* [[prism (geometry)|prism]]s, for each rational number ''p/q'' &gt; 2, with symmetry group '''D<sub>''p''h</sub>''';
* [[antiprism]]s, for each rational number ''p/q'' &gt; 3/2, with symmetry group '''D<sub>''p''d</sub>''' if ''q'' is odd, '''D<sub>''p''h</sub>''' if ''q'' is even.

If ''p/q'' is an integer, i.e. if ''q'' = 1, the prism or antiprism is convex.  (The fraction is always assumed to be stated in lowest terms.)

An antiprism with ''p/q'' &lt; 2 is ''crossed'' or ''retrograde''; its [[vertex figure]] resembles a bowtie.  If ''p/q'' &lt; 3/2 no uniform antiprism can exist, as its vertex figure would have to violate the [[triangle inequality]]. If ''p/q'' = 3/2 the uniform antiprism is degenerate (has zero height).

Note: The [[tetrahedron]], [[cube]], and [[octahedron]] are listed here with dihedral symmetry (as a ''digonal antiprism'', ''square prism'' and ''triangular antiprism'' respectively), although if uniformly colored, the tetrahedron also has tetrahedral symmetry and the cube and octahedron also have octahedral symmetry.
